predecessors.name: Hittite Empire
predecessors.text: 'south-central Anatolia'; the page's proposed sites (Turkmen-Karahoyuk on the Konya Plain, Konya, Sirkeli Hoyuk in Cilicia, Kilise Tepe, Kizildag, Meydancik) span the Konya Plain to the Mersin coast…

ledger.x: Early 13th century BC: Muwatalli II makes Tarhuntassa the Hittite capital.
13th century BC (bridged): Hattusili III makes Tarhuntassa a vassal kingdom.
Toward the end of the Hittite empire (bridged to c.

c. 1180 BC (bridged): the page is silent on what followed Tarhuntassa. It names no successor state; the Hartapu inscription at Turkmen-Karahoyuk dates to the 12th or 8th century BC (excavators say 8th).

wars.name: Hatti's attack on Tarhuntassa under Suppiluliuma II
wars.outcome: 'Toward the end of the Hittite empire' Suppiluliuma II recorded that Hatti attacked and sacked Tarhuntassa.

certainty.note: The capital's site is unknown and the page describes no border; the shape is a regional reading from proposed sites.
